title: Sanjay Dutt at 67: Six Meals a Day and a Weakness for Biryani
excerpt: As Bollywood's 'Baba' marks his 67th birthday, a look at the disciplined six-meal diet that keeps him camera-ready — and the cheat-day indulgences he refuses to give up.
body:
• Sanjay Dutt follows a structured six-meal-a-day diet built around muesli, egg whites, avocado, boiled chicken, and grilled vegetables.
  • The actor's go-to cheat meals — biryani, shaami kebab, and boti kebab — reflect his deep roots in Mughlai culinary traditions.
  • At 67, Dutt combines disciplined eating with consistent gym work, favouring compound lifts, resistance bands, and treadmill runs over flashy routines.
  • Beyond personal eating habits, Dutt has expanded into food entrepreneurship with his Dubai-based brand Franktea and the Mumbai restaurant Solaire.

Sanjay Dutt turned 67 on July 29, and the Bollywood veteran marked the occasion by doing what he does most mornings — eating a bowl of muesli, followed by egg whites and avocado, then heading to the gym. The man known across India as "Sanju Baba" has built his late-career physical presence on a regimented six-meal-a-day eating plan that prioritises lean protein, controlled portions, and timing over calorie counting.

The Six-Meal Blueprint

In a widely shared interview on Curly Tales' Sunday Brunch with host Kamiya Jani, Dutt laid out his daily diet in detail. He breaks his eating into six small portions spaced across the day, beginning with muesli or oats paired with fruit for slow-release carbohydrates. A mid-morning snack of egg whites and avocado supplies lean protein and healthy fats.

"As per the workout, one should have six small meals a day."

— Sanjay Dutt, in an interview with Curly Tales

Lunch centres on boiled chicken with quinoa or brown rice and greens. An afternoon snack of mixed fruits or a protein smoothie bridges the gap before dinner, which typically features grilled vegetables with paneer or a light fish preparation. If he is still hungry late at night, Dutt reaches for herbal tea or a handful of almonds.

The approach is a textbook example of the "grazing" strategy favoured by fitness professionals — keeping blood sugar stable, managing appetite, and sustaining energy through long shoot days. Nutritionists note that six evenly spaced meals can help maintain metabolic rate, particularly for older adults trying to preserve muscle mass.

Biryani, Kebabs, and the Art of the Cheat Day

When Jani asked Dutt about his cheat-day favourites, the actor's restrained demeanour crumbled. "Biryani," he said immediately, before rattling off shaami kebab and boti kebab with undisguised enthusiasm. Jani's reaction — "This is very boring. Humne ye to nahi expect kiya tha aapse" — had come in response to his clean-eating routine, but the cheat-day confession was anything but boring.

"For actors, being fit is very important for us."

— Sanjay Dutt

Dutt's indulgences are not random fast-food detours. They trace a direct line to the Mughlai kitchen traditions of his family. His mother, the legendary actress Nargis Dutt, was known for her home-cooked rogan josh and shami kebab. "Growing up, it was all about my mom's home-cooked rogan josh and shami kebab. Those flavours are still my comfort food," Dutt has said in earlier interviews. The biryani-and-kebab cheat day is, in some ways, an act of culinary memory.

The Gym at 67

Diet is only half the equation. Dutt's fitness routine at 67 leans toward consistency rather than intensity. Insiders told Mobile Masala that his gym sessions are built around compound lifts, resistance bands, light dumbbells, and treadmill runs. He works out regularly — not for vanity, but for what he describes as functional longevity. "Going to the gym and being fit is very important," Dutt has said, particularly in the film industry where physical demands remain high regardless of age.

His approach contrasts with the high-intensity regimes associated with younger Bollywood actors. There are no dramatic transformation montages or social-media workout reels — just steady, unsexy work repeated day after day. At an age when many actors transition to purely advisory roles, Dutt continues to take on physically demanding parts, most recently in the Telugu film circuit.

From the Plate to the Business

Dutt's relationship with food extends beyond his own kitchen. In late 2024, he and his wife Maanayata launched Dutt's Franktea in Dubai, a delivery-focused food brand offering fusion rolls paired with kadak chai. Available through Talabat UAE, the venture blends international flavours with Indian culinary sensibilities — what Maanayata described as "in-house recipes curated tastefully, blended with international flavours and desi love."

In Mumbai, Dutt is also behind Solaire, a restaurant that has attracted attention for its cross-cultural menu featuring items like Kerala fried chicken with peanut pesto, Bombay duck roulettes with Goan recheado, and lamb kebab with chimichurri. It is the kind of menu that reflects exactly how Dutt eats — rooted in Indian flavour traditions but open to global influence.

And then there is the dish he did not create but that bears his name: Chicken Sanju Baba, a fixture at Noor Mohammadi Hotel on Mumbai's Mohammed Ali Road. Dutt reportedly shared the recipe with the restaurant owner years ago. "The real credit goes to the chefs who created it," he has said. "Mumbai has a vibrant food scene, and it's an honour to be a part of it."

What Comes Next

At 67, Dutt shows no signs of softening his discipline. The six-meal structure has become less a diet and more a lifestyle architecture — one that accommodates biryani cravings without derailing the larger plan. For a generation of Indian men entering their 60s and beyond, his approach offers a practical template: eat small, eat clean, stay active, and keep a plate of biryani in the rotation.
nri_angle: Dutt's diet bridges Indian culinary heritage — his mother Nargis's rogan josh, Mughlai kebabs, and biryani — with modern wellness practices familiar to diaspora audiences balancing desi food traditions with healthy eating.
